sections.html:
Cedar Rapids is the Linn County seat and the second most populous city in Iowa, with 137,710 residents at the 2020 count and 137,935 in mid-2025. It lies about 20 miles north of Iowa City and 128 miles northeast of Des Moines.

Addresses fall into four quadrants. The Cedar River divides east from west, and 1st Avenue (U.S. Route 151 Business) divides north from south. The city uses 14 ZIP codes, and downtown and Mays Island are in 52401. When you describe a house to anyone, give the quadrant and ZIP along with the street, because buyers search that way and the quadrant tells them which neighborhood and often which school district they are looking at.

Two kinds of storm left their mark on Cedar Rapids housing, river water and wind. Buyers know both stories, so expect questions.

  • June 2008 flood: the Cedar River crested at a record 31.12 feet on June 13, well above the previous record of 20 feet. About 1,126 city blocks flooded, 7,749 properties were evacuated, 5,900 of them homes, and at least 1,300 properties were demolished.
  • September 2016 flood: the river reached 22 feet on September 27, the second highest crest on record against a flood stage of 12 feet. More than 5,000 homes were affected. The city had approved a $625 million, 20-year levee plan the year before.
  • August 10, 2020 derecho: winds of 60 to 80 mph, with gusts of 110 mph or more, knocked out power to about 95 percent of the city and damaged 20 schools.

If your house sits where water or wind did damage, a conventional buyer's inspector will look hard at the basement, the roof and the electrical system. Gather repair receipts and insurance paperwork before you talk price. A cash purchase lets you skip the back and forth over repair credits.

Twelve neighborhood associations are active in the city. Those nearest downtown include Wellington Heights, Oakhill Jackson and Moundview, and other named areas include Noelridge Park and Kenwood Park. Informal districts such as Czech Village, New Bohemia (NewBo), Kingston Village and Wilderness Estates also come up in listings.

Four school districts reach into the city, and your address decides which applies:

  • Cedar Rapids Community School District, with 15,589 students in 2023-24, 21 elementary schools, 6 middle schools and 5 high schools.
  • Linn-Mar Community School District, which covers part of the northeast quadrant.
  • College Community School District, which covers part of the southwest quadrant.
  • Marion Independent School District, which covers a portion of the city.

Families ask about the district before almost anything else, so check it for your street and state it accurately.

A rental house in Cedar Rapids must hold a Certificate of Compliance before anyone can legally live in it. The city issues the certificate once the property meets the Housing Code and the registration and inspection charges are paid.

Rental typeAnnual registration fee
Single-family unit or condominium$50
Duplex$60
Multi-family structure$42 plus $13 per unit

A separate inspection fee schedule took effect July 1, 2023. The full list is on the city's rental housing page.

A landlord who is done managing a rental can sell it with tenants in place or after they move out. Ask the buyer whether the registration will carry over or has to be filed fresh, and call the city's housing inspections office to confirm before closing.

sections.h2: What Iowa requires at a Cedar Rapids closing
sections.html:
Each deed that goes through the Linn County Recorder carries a declaration of value, and most also carry a groundwater hazard statement. Iowa Code 558.69 lays out what the seller reports:

  • Wells, with their approximate location and whether they meet state rules.
  • Private burial sites, underground storage tanks and known hazardous waste.
  • Solid waste disposal sites identified by the Department of Natural Resources.
  • Private sewage disposal systems, and whether they were inspected or are exempt at transfer.

At least one seller, or the seller's agent, signs the statement and the buyer gets a copy. You are responsible for the accuracy of your answers. After the 2008 flood, owners of older properties should dig through their records for any tank or well that was removed, capped or replaced, since an old note can settle a question quickly.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Cedar Rapids house work?
sections.html:
Selling for cash means no repairs, no showings and no lender appraisal. The steps are short.

  1. Send the address and a few details about the condition and any tenants.
  2. Receive a written offer based on the house as it stands.
  3. If the offer works for you, pick a closing date and let a title company prepare the deed, declaration of value and groundwater statement.
  4. Close, and record the deed at the county.

You can say no to an offer at no cost. Compare it with what a listing would net after repairs, the wait for a buyer and the cost of carrying the house in the meantime.

sections.h2: Property taxes owed at the sale
sections.html:
Iowa property tax comes in two installments that turn delinquent on October 1 and April 1 under Iowa Code 445.37. Ask the Linn County Treasurer what is paid before the closing date, so the title company can divide the current bill between you and the buyer.

Bring the latest tax statement to the first conversation with a buyer. A paid-up house closes faster, and an installment that is already delinquent is something to raise early rather than at the closing table.

If the house is a rental, also bring the Certificate of Compliance and the latest registration receipt. Buyers who plan to keep renting want to know what carries over and what restarts, and the paperwork answers that in a minute.

sections.h2: Getting a house ready for a cash offer
sections.html:
You do not have to repair a Cedar Rapids house to sell it for cash, but a little preparation makes an offer more accurate. Walk through the basement first, since that is where flood and storm history show up most. Note any past water, any sump pump or drain work, and what the roof looked like after the 2020 derecho.

Next, write down what you know about wells, tanks and septic systems, because the groundwater statement asks for those facts. Then pull together the deed, any survey and the tenant lease if there is one. The more complete the picture you give a buyer, the closer the first offer will be to the final number.

faqs.q: How many people live in Cedar Rapids?
faqs.a: The 2020 count was 137,710 residents, and the mid-2025 estimate is 137,935. It is the second most populous city in Iowa.

faqs.q: How high did the Cedar River get in the 2008 flood?
faqs.a: It crested at a record 31.12 feet on June 13, 2008, against an earlier record of 20 feet. In all, 7,749 properties were evacuated, including 5,900 homes.

faqs.q: Do landlords need a permit in Cedar Rapids?
faqs.a: Yes. Rental housing needs a Certificate of Compliance to be occupied legally. Registration runs $50 a year for a single-family unit or condo, $60 for a duplex, and $42 plus $13 per unit for multi-family buildings.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Cedar Rapids house in?
faqs.a: It depends on the address. Cedar Rapids Community Schools covers most of the city, while Linn-Mar, College Community and Marion Independent each cover part of it.

faqs.q: What do I disclose about wells or tanks in Cedar Rapids?
faqs.a: Iowa Code 558.69 has the seller report wells, burial sites, underground tanks, hazardous waste, solid waste disposal sites and private sewage systems on a groundwater hazard statement filed with the deed.
